case_title.reason: Title matches the judgment caption, Shiva Kumar @ Shiva @ Shivamurthy v. State of Karnataka.

number_of_accused.reason: Single appellant accused; the judgment refers only to 'the appellant'.

accused_gender.reason: Accused is referred to as male throughout ('his life', 'he').

accused_age.reason: Trial Court noted age 27 on conviction; the value matches that finding, though age at offence was 22.

accused_religion.reason: Religion is not mentioned in the judgment.

accused_caste.reason: Caste is not mentioned in the judgment.

accused_occupation.reason: Judgment describes the appellant as the driver of the company vehicle.

accused_socioeconomic_status.reason: Socioeconomic status is not discussed in the judgment.

previous_criminal_record.reason: Judgment states the accused has no antecedents and this was his first offence.

victim_gender.reason: Victim is the deceased woman; judgment refers to her as a woman.

victim_age.reason: Judgment states the victim's life was cut short at age 28.

victim_caste.reason: Caste is not mentioned in the judgment.

victim_religion.reason: Religion is not mentioned in the judgment.

accused_victim_relationship.quote: the appellant, who was the driver
accused_victim_relationship.reason: Judgment never describes the relationship as stranger; the accused was her company cab driver who offered a lift.

offence_category.correct_value: Rape and murder (with kidnapping/abduction under s.366)
offence_category.quote: The appellant has been convicted for the offences punishable under Sections 366, 376 and 302
offence_category.reason: Omits the murder (s.302) and abduction (s.366) convictions, which are central to the case.

statutory_provisions.quote: offences punishable under Sections 366, 376 and 302 of the Indian Penal Code
statutory_provisions.reason: Omits section 366, under which the appellant was also convicted.

weapon.reason: No weapon is mentioned in the judgment.

evidence_type.correct_value: Recovery of body, clothes and footwear; prosecution evidence establishing rape and murder
evidence_type.quote: her dead body was recovered at the instance of the appellant
evidence_type.reason: Recovery is supported, but medical evidence is not mentioned anywhere in the judgment.

confession.quote: her dead body was recovered at the instance of the appellant
confession.reason: Judgment does not mention any confession; asserting 'None' is not backed by the text.

aggravating_circumstances.correct_value: Brutal nature of the crime; shock to judicial conscience; undue leniency would erode public confidence
aggravating_circumstances.quote: The facts are such, which will shock the conscience of any Court.
aggravating_circumstances.reason: Judgment clearly identifies aggravating features, including brutality and public confidence concerns.

mitigating_circumstances.correct_value: Age 27 at conviction; wife, small child and aged parents; first offence; no antecedents; possibility of reformation
mitigating_circumstances.quote: he had a wife and small child as well as aged parents
mitigating_circumstances.reason: Judgment lists several mitigating factors, including family circumstances, first offence and reformation.

trial_court_outcome.reason: Sessions Judge sentenced appellant to rigorous imprisonment for the rest of his life, as stated.

high_court_outcome.correct_value: High Court dismissed both the accused's appeal against conviction and sentence and the State's enhancement appeal
high_court_outcome.quote: The High Court, by the impugned judgment, dismissed both appeals.
high_court_outcome.reason: Judgment states the High Court dismissed both appeals, not 'Not applicable'.

final_outcome.correct_value: Convicted under ss.366, 376 and 302; sentence modified to life imprisonment with release only after 30 years of actual sentence
final_outcome.quote: The appeal is partly allowed to the above extent.
final_outcome.reason: 'Convicted' is right but omits the Supreme Court's partial allowance modifying the sentence.

offence_finally_established.quote: The prosecution successfully established the charge of the offence of rape
offence_finally_established.reason: Omits the murder conviction under s.302 and the s.366 conviction, both upheld.

imprisonment_type.reason: Court imposed a fixed-term sentence of thirty years as a modified life sentence.

imprisonment_years.reason: Court directed release only after thirty years of actual sentence.

fine_rs.reason: No fine is mentioned in the judgment.

neutral_facts.correct_value: Neutral facts without the statement that the prosecution established rape, which reveals the trial finding
neutral_facts.quote: The prosecution successfully established the charge of the offence of rape
neutral_facts.reason: Facts are accurate, but stating the prosecution established rape reveals the conviction outcome.

offence_severity.reason: Judgment refers to death penalty or life imprisonment as punishments for the grave offence.

attempt_completion.reason: Judgment states the victim was raped and killed, so offences were completed.

physical_harm.reason: Judgment describes rape and murder resulting in the victim's death.

number_of_offences.reason: Convictions under ss.366, 376 and 302 were upheld by the High Court and not disturbed.

financial_property_loss.reason: Judgment does not discuss any financial or property loss.

premeditation_planning.reason: Judgment does not state premeditation or planning.

motive.reason: Judgment does not identify any motive.

key_evidence_accepted.reason: Judgment states the prosecution established rape and the s.302 conviction stands.

witness_credibility.quote: The maternal uncle of the deceased lodged a complaint
witness_credibility.reason: Judgment contains no assessment of witness credibility; the claimed analysis is not in the text.

post_offence_conduct.correct_value: Counsel submitted satisfactory conduct in jail and completion of a B.A. degree while in jail
post_offence_conduct.quote: his conduct in jail is all throughout satisfactory and in fact, he has completed B.A. degree course while in jail
post_offence_conduct.reason: Jail conduct is recorded in counsel's submissions, so 'Not stated' misses this material.

custody_duration.correct_value: Approximately seventeen years and two months of sentence served (per appellant's counsel)
custody_duration.quote: the appellant has undergone sentence for approximately seventeen years and two months
custody_duration.reason: Judgment states the custody duration, so 'Not stated' is wrong.

bail_history.reason: Bail history is not discussed in the judgment.

trial_duration.correct_value: High Court decision: May 31, 2016; Supreme Court decision: March 28, 2023; offence and trial dates not stated
trial_duration.quote: Judgment and Order dated 31.05.2016 of the High Court
trial_duration.reason: High Court judgment date of 31.05.2016 is stated in the judgment but recorded as 'Not stated'.

investigation_status.reason: Investigation status is not discussed in the judgment.

appeal_history.correct_value: High Court dismissed the accused's appeal and the State's enhancement appeal; Supreme Court partly allowed the appeal and modified sentence
appeal_history.quote: The High Court, by the impugned judgment, dismissed both appeals.
appeal_history.reason: Omits that the High Court also dismissed the State's enhancement appeal.

prosecution_argument.reason: Matches the State's submission that Constitutional Courts are not powerless to impose modified sentences.

defence_argument.reason: Matches the appellant's reliance on Sriharan and on modified sentences only in commutation cases.

legal_principle_applied.correct_value: Constitutional Courts can impose a fixed-term or modified sentence even where capital punishment is not imposed or proposed
legal_principle_applied.quote: the Constitutional Courts can always exercise the power of imposing a modified or fixed-term sentence
legal_principle_applied.reason: Recites the Sriharan restriction, but the Court's applied principle is that Constitutional Courts may impose fixed terms without death penalty.

precedent_relied_upon.reason: All four cases are cited in the judgment as followed, referred to, or relied upon.

sentencing_rationale.quote: it can always impose a fixed-term sentence so that the benefit of statutory remission, etc. is not available to the accused
sentencing_rationale.reason: Matches the reasoning in paragraphs 12 and 16 on gravity and remission.

judicial_mitigating_factors.reason: Trial Court's age, family circumstances and first offence are recorded as mitigating factors.

judicial_aggravating_factors.reason: Brutality, shock to conscience and public confidence concerns are all noted by the Court.

other_sentence_order.reason: Matches the operative direction for life imprisonment with release only after thirty years.
